payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_follow_up.py::test_a_draft_sent_back_once_pools_on_its_second_refusal_and_never_past_the_sub_cap stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'A second parse failure charges the first session again, not the second.' applied to saffron/follow_up.py as an edit. The claim was "A group is sent back at most once. When its second draft also fails to parse, it pools with `follow-up text did not parse: ` and the second draft's error, and no third call is made. A second session that sets a reset time, carries an error, or raises is handled as a first one is. A reset time pools its group and every later group. An error pools the group with it. A raise from the second call pools the group with `write raised`, and the raise goes no further. A second draft `_validate` refuses for its type pools with that reason. A first draft `_validate` refuses for its id, type, `depends_on`, budget or `touches` pools after one call, never sent back. Every session but the raised one is charged to the origin task, once each. The witness reads the origin's `WRITING` attempts' session ids in order. Both sessions' costs count against `cap_usd`. The send-back is priced after the first session's cost is counted. When what is left cannot cover `SPEC_WRITER_SESSION_USD`, the group pools with its first draft's parse reason and no second call is made. The witness's sub-cap run makes that true only once each session's cost is counted.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_follow_up.py::test_a_follow_up_writers_attempt_records_the_model_its_session_names, tests/test_follow_up.py::test_a_draft_that_does_not_parse_is_sent_back_once_with_its_error_and_then_minted, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
